source: Position and Displacement on an Axis
Pick an origin and a positive direction; displacement Δx = x_final − x_initial carries a sign.
Students compute displacement as the total distance traveled, ignoring a change of direction.

In Distance and Displacement you met the difference between how far you went and where you ended up. To work with numbers, physicists put the motion on an axis: pick an origin ($x = 0$) and a positive direction. Then every position is a signed number, like the integers in Subtracting Integers.

Displacement is final position minus initial position: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$. Its sign tells the direction: positive means it ended up on the $+x$ side of where it started, negative means the $-x$ side.

Subtraction measures the gap between two numbers on a number line, including which way you step to get from the first to the second. Going from $x = 2$ to $x = 7$ is a step of $+5$; going from $7$ back to $2$ is a step of $-5$. Displacement is exactly that step, for the whole trip at once, so it ignores everything that happened in between.
The cart starts at x = 4 m, rolls right, stops and comes back past where it started. The odometer adds every meter; the displacement only compares the end with the start.
Worked examples
A cart starts at $x = 3\ \text{m}$ and stops at $x = -5\ \text{m}$. Find its displacement.
A move to the left
$\Delta x = -8\ \text{m}$
$\Delta x = x_f - x_i = -5 - 3$.
$\Delta x = -8\ \text{m}$. The minus sign says it moved 8 m in the $-x$ direction.
A runner goes from $x = 10\ \text{m}$ to $x = 70\ \text{m}$, then turns and jogs back to $x = 40\ \text{m}$. Find the displacement and the distance.
Out and back
$\Delta x = 30\ \text{m}$; distance $= 90\ \text{m}$.
Displacement uses only the ends: $\Delta x = 40 - 10 = 30\ \text{m}$.
Distance adds the length of every leg: $60\ \text{m}$ out and $30\ \text{m}$ back.
Distance $= 60 + 30 = 90\ \text{m}$.

Using the total distance as the displacement. When the motion changes direction, the two differ: the runner above traveled 90 m but is only 30 m from the start. Check: displacement can be negative or zero; distance never can. If an object ends where it began, its displacement is zero however far it went.
